candidates.passage: Machine Learning Based Intrusion Detection System This project builds an intrusion detection system that classifies network traffic as normal or malicious. It replaces fixed signature rules with a trained model, so it can flag attacks that no existing rule describes. The system captures packets, groups them into flows, and extracts features such as flow duration, packet counts, and byte rates. A random forest classifier was trained on the CICIDS2017 dataset and reached 97 percent accuracy on held-out traffic. When the model flags a flow, the system writes an alert to a log file with the source address, the destination address, and the predicted attack type. Administrators review these alerts on a simple dashboard.
